resources.string: Join your iPhone’s Personal Hotspot in the Wi‑Fi settings

To show your iPhone’s screen as soon as mirroring starts, allow AirPlay Car to display over other apps.

This head unit does not offer that setting in its menus. It can be enabled once from a computer:

adb shell appops set %1$s SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow
AirPlay Car %1$s is the latest version.
GitHub could not be reached. Check that the head unit has internet (for example through the iPhone’s hotspot) and try again.
This release has no package for this head unit (%1$s).
To install updates, allow AirPlay Car to install apps on the next screen. The update continues when you come back.
On iPhone, tap AirPlay and choose “%1$s”
On iPhone: Control Center → Screen Mirroring → %1$s
Turn on Personal Hotspot on your iPhone and join it here once. The head unit joins it again by itself on every drive.
The receiver could not start. Restart the head unit or export diagnostics in Settings → Advanced.
Mirroring the screen. Siri and the steering wheel buttons work as usual.
On the iPhone: Settings → Personal Hotspot → Allow Others to Join. Keep it on; the iPhone uses almost no power for it while nothing is connected.
Join it from the head unit
Choose your iPhone in the head unit’s Wi‑Fi list and enter the hotspot password. From then on the head unit joins it by itself when the car starts, and it gets internet for maps and updates.
Let the picture open by itself
Allow AirPlay Car to display over other apps, so the iPhone’s screen appears as soon as you start mirroring, whatever is on the head unit.
Screen: Control Center → Screen Mirroring → %1$s. Music only: the AirPlay button in any player → %1$s. The iPhone remembers the choice for the next drive.

Turn off Portrait Orientation Lock in Control Center: navigators that turn sideways, such as Yandex Navigator, Google Maps and 2GIS, then fill the whole screen. Upright, the map stands next to the dock at full height. Keep the iPhone on a charger; navigators keep it unlocked by themselves, and their voice comes through the car’s speakers.
In the Shortcuts app: Automation → New → Bluetooth → your car (or Wi‑Fi) → action “Set Playback Destination” → %1$s, then “Play/Pause” → Play. Turn off “Ask Before Running”.

Touches on the head unit do not reach the iPhone: Apple’s screen mirroring carries the picture and sound only. Use Siri, the iPhone itself, or the controls here and on the steering wheel, which pause and skip the music.
